supporting_observations.claim: At 13:37 UTC, WS-TWEBER-01 exchanged Kerberos and LDAP traffic with the domain controller; these records do not identify an account-creation operation or the user performing it.
At 13:42 UTC, the available records show WS-TWEBER-01 using the proxy for a Google Update tunnel, not an account-management event.

At 13:56 UTC, emma.stone launched Remote Desktop to WS-TWEBER-01 and an explicit-credentials event names tom.weber as the target user; these records do not establish that a session succeeded or that it was related to the alerted account.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on both WS-TWEBER-01 and DC-PIN-01 from 13:25 through 14:20 UTC, overlapping the alert time and preventing review of relevant host and domain-controller events.
The supplied network records show connections and protocols but do not establish whether it_support was created, who created it, or what privileges or group memberships it received.
claims_not_established: The supplied records do not independently confirm the creation of it_support or establish its exact creation time.
The creator, source host, authorization, intended purpose, enabled status, and group or privilege assignments of it_support are not established.
The records do not establish whether the account was used after creation or whether any activity was malicious.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve DC-PIN-01 Security and directory audit events for the alert window, including account creation, group membership changes, and the initiating subject and source workstation.
Recover WS-TWEBER-01 Security and Sysmon logs for the window, including account-management events and process or logon context.
Verify it_support in Active Directory: creation time, creator/subject if available, enabled state, group memberships, privileges, and subsequent authentication or use.
Check the change or help-desk records for authorization and purpose for creating it_support.
unrelated_findings: WS-ESTONE-01 launched Remote Desktop to WS-TWEBER-01 and recorded explicit credentials targeting tom.weber at 13:56 UTC. This may merit separate review against the remote-administration practice, but the records do not show a successful session or connect it to the alerted account. (T077-00129, T077-00130, T077-00131)
